newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU finance ministers agree to readmit lira at 990 to mark.
newsitem.headline: EU finance ministers agree to readmit lira at 990 to mark.

text.p: Finance ministers and central bank governors from the European Union, meeting in emergency session, agreed Sunday to readmit the Italian lira to the EU's exchange rate mechanism.
European Union officials said the ministers agreed to allow the lira to return to the currency grid at a rate of 990 lira to the German mark, rather than the 1,000 lira that Rome had been seeking.
The agreement came after an eight-hour meeting at which EU countries made it clear to Rome that they were not willing to see the lira re-enter the currency grid at a weak rate.
European countries worried that entering at a weaker rate would give Italy preferential trade terms.

Europe's top financial policy-makers had to be called in to consider the issue after a Saturday meeting of the EU's monetary committee of central bank and finance ministry officials failed to agree on a rate for the lira's return.

Italy originally had been pressing on Saturday for a rate of 1,010 lira to the mark and then lowered its sights to 1,000 Sunday in an attempt to win agreement, but it still could not win over its EU partners.
After the meeting dragged on into the night, the finance ministers and central bankers finally settled on 990 lira to the mark, diplomats said.
Germany and France had led the opposition to a higher level, arguing that the Italian government was trying to bring the lira back at too weak a rate, a diplomat said.

Rejoining the exchange rate mechanism -- from which the lira was unceremoniously dumped amid a currency crisis in 1992 -- is seen as crucial for Italy's hopes for being in the first wave of EU countries to adopt a single currency in 1999.
A stable two-year stint within the exchange rate mechanism -- designed to provide exchange rate stability -- is one of the qualifying criteria for the new currency, the Euro.
Italy's failure to win a seat within the exchange rate mechanism would have put pressure on the lira and sent a strong negative signal over the prospect of a joint European currency.
But Italy was not in a strong position at the meeting because of what might happen to the lira if it was not let back in at all.
